previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, calciphylaxis, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for fever and worsening kidney function. He had recently been treated for necrotizing fasciitis and was on multiple medications, including immunosuppressants. Upon admission, his fever resolved without evidence of infection, and blood cultures were negative. His elevated creatinine was attributed to dehydration and chronic kidney damage from hypertension and vascular disease, confirmed by a kidney biopsy showing glomerulosclerosis and arteriosclerosis without rejection. Blood pressure was initially severe but improved with optimization of antihypertensives, including increasing the clonidine patch and holding nephrotoxic agents. The left leg wound showed granulation tissue but persistent tendon exposure, prompting outpatient plastic surgery follow-up. Wound care was transitioned to wet-to-dry dressings. Pain medications were adjusted for renal function, and he was discharged home with home health services and close follow-up planned.

Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY:
==========
Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o man with a PMH of ESRD ___ 
diabetic nephropathy s/p failed renal transplant in ___ and s/p 
DDRT in ___ c/b BK viremia, on leflunomide), recent diagnosis 
of calciphylaxis on sodium thiosulfate, Hypertension, IDDM, 
chronic hand wounds, and recent complex admission for 
necrotizing fasciitis underlying left lower extremity 
calciphylaxis wound requiring debridement, wound vac, and course 
of IV Zosyn with recent admission for fever and ___ who 
presented with confusion. 

# TOXIC METABOLIC ENCEPHALOPATHY
The patient presented with acute onset confusion reported by his 
sisters who live with him that he was forgetful and urinated in 
his room thinking he was at the urinal when he was not. The most 
likely etiology for confusion was opioid toxicity, as the 
patient's mental status cleared over his first day of admission 
after decreasing the dose of opioids. Other considerations were 
infection, however, workup was negative. Vascular dementia was 
considered but unlikely as symptoms resolved. Despite positive 
amphetamines on admission, there was a low clinical suspicion 
for amphetamine use, as he has had false positives in the past 
due to labetalol. 

# HISTORY OF NECROTIZING FASCIITIS, LLE 
# CHRONIC HAND WOUNDS 
The patient was noted to have a chronic wound on his left leg 
that appeared stable from prior. Vascular surgery saw the 
patient and although they were concerned by several areas of 
necrotic eschar, they did not think the wound was actively 
infected. He is scheduled to see plastic surgery as an 
outpatient for ongoing followup. Dry gangrene of left hand due 
to severe peripheral vascular disease and calciphylaxis, but no 
evidence of active infection. 

# ESRD S/P DDRT.

thiosulfate while admitted. Discharge creatinine 2.5
